chunks: And from him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

If the enslaved person entering into a contract of manumission (mukatab) stipulates upon his master that there is no right of patronage (walayah) for anyone upon him if he pays the money, and the one who contracted with him acknowledges this, then there is no right of patronage for anyone upon him.
And if the master stipulates the patronage of the mukatab, and the one who was contracted with (the master) acknowledges it, then the patronage belongs to him.

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ الْمُكَاتَبُ: The enslaved person who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum in exchange for freedom.
key_terms.الْوَلَاءَ: The right of patronage or kinship that typically attaches to a freed slave, granting the master certain social and legal claims.

ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions for waiving or retaining the right of patronage (walayah) in a slave's contract of manumission?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the mukatab contract, emphasizing that the right of walayah (patronage) is a negotiable asset rather than an immutable status. It highlights the principle of contractual autonomy in Shia jurisprudence, where the specific stipulations agreed upon by both parties determine the post-emancipation relationship, reflecting the practical legal mechanisms used to facilitate slave manumission in early Islamic society.
